root_cause_label: Agent misread the cost model mechanics: all six packer iterations grouped requests only by prompt_len, never operationalizing that G_max within each batch drives decode-phase padding and that gen_len homogeneity is the critical batching axis
one_sentence_failure_summary: After reading the cost model the agent failed to internalize that decode-phase padding is dominated by G_max per batch, so all six subsequent batching algorithms clustered solely by prompt_len similarity without gen_len-aware batch splitting, leaving pad_ratio and latency thresholds unmet at submission.
t_err_evidence: cat /app/task_file/scripts/cost_model.py; agent reads cost model that it later misuses to drive seq_align selection.
t_commit_evidence: Step 14: agent writes improved_packer.py — the first concrete implementation — sorting by prompt_len only with no gen_len splitting. This wrong-axis decision is literally copied into every subsequent script (advanced, refined, targeted, optimized, final, tuned). After step 14 no attempt to pivot toward a gen_len-first batching axis is ever made, locking in the failure.
t_surface_evidence: Pad Ratio: 0.5704 ... 0.7392; improved plan still far above target thresholds after the new strategy.
trigger_explanation: The agent read cost_model.py at step 6 and saw the decode-padding formula pad_decode = sum(G_max - r['gen_len'] for r in reqs_list), which makes clear that G_max within a batch is the dominant lever. The agent's verbal interpretation acknowledged gen_len 'matters' but then wrote six algorithms that cluster exclusively by prompt_len without any gen_len-range splitting. This is a misread of the output of its own exploration: the evidence for the correct strategy was present in the code it read but not correctly translated into an implementation plan.
